claims.statement: From 18 February 2027, the EU Batteries Regulation requires each light-means-of-transport battery placed on the market or put into service to have an electronic battery passport.

The European Commission describes the battery passport as covering e-bike and e-scooter batteries and supporting access to performance, repair, reuse, and recycling information across the value chain.
Hypothesis: a trusted used-battery condition credential can raise dealer conversion or reduce returns enough to support per-test fees; this must be measured in a controlled dealer pilot.

contrary_evidence: The mandatory passport applies to batteries newly placed on the market and may not provide complete histories for older used stock.
Manufacturer battery-management data and simple capacity testers may already be enough for some dealers.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: equip five high-volume refurbishers, measure return-rate and days-to-sale changes, then recruit marketplaces that require or highlight the credential.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 50 shops and 12000 tests in year 2, 400 shops and 150000 tests in year 5, then EU marketplace APIs producing 12-20M PLN annual revenue. At 15% operating margin, a 3-4x revenue value, and 50-65% founder ownership, equity could exceed 5M PLN; marketplace acceptance is the decisive milestone.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 15-20 hours/week with battery safety testing delegated to qualified shop technicians.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 60-72% during technician-led testing, rising above 80% for software/API revenue; hardware remains shop-owned or leased.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 5-9 months on 4000-7000 PLN acquisition and onboarding cost for a shop producing 60 paid tests monthly.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 79-149 PLN per test, 299 PLN/month shop software, and API fees for marketplace verification.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: repeat follows every used-bike intake and battery replacement; marketplace acceptance should improve issuer retention and test volume.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Model-, age-, usage-, repair-, and return-linked degradation dataset plus a growing installed network of credential issuers and acceptors
fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish e-bike dealers, repair shops, refurbishers, and used-bike marketplaces
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Repair-shop certification, marketplace listing integrations, and insurer/refurbisher acceptance of the passport
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Standardized battery test, signed condition record, residual-value band, and passport API sold per transaction
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Dealer or refurbisher pays per completed diagnostic passport and optionally a shop subscription
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A used e-bike is acquired, listed, financed, insured, returned, or its battery is replaced

founder_fit: Data science supports degradation curves and residual-value modeling.
A shop-led protocol avoids a camera-facing consumer brand.
Can start in Warsaw with rented or partner test equipment below the founder's capital ceiling.
Combines quantified-condition data with a repeat transaction credential.
risks: Battery fire or injury if a test is performed incorrectly; certified procedures and liability cover are essential.
The credential must not be marketed as an official EU conformity decision.
OEM lock-in or inaccessible battery-management data.

structure.control_point: signed used-battery condition record accepted in resale workflows
structure.critical_dependency: validated cross-model testing protocol and acceptance by resale intermediaries

thesis: A diagnostic and provenance network for used e-bike batteries. Independent repair shops run a standardized state-of-health and safety protocol, issue a signed resale credential linked to the EU battery passport where available, and feed anonymized degradation and return outcomes into model-specific residual-value benchmarks.
title: SecondRide Battery Health Passport
uncertainties: A safe, repeatable protocol across proprietary battery-management systems requires technical validation.
Marketplace, insurer, and dealer acceptance of a third-party condition credential is unknown.
The 75000 PLN capital estimate and all pricing, adoption, payback, and valuation figures below are planning hypotheses.
